subject: When to use plyr's rename function instead of dplyr's

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: When to use plyr's rename function instead of dplyr's
parts:
Hi All,

I just tried out the new rename() function in dplyr, which works like select() but keeps even the variables you didn't ask for or rename. It's a nice addition to dplyr and it fits in well with how dplyr works. However, it may not always be the best way to rename variables. The plyr package also has a rename() function, and it uses R's built-in names() function. So if you had a large data set and all you wanted to do was rename some variables (perhaps to match names before stacking the data set with another via rbind() or rbind_list()), it would be much more efficient to use plyr's rename() as the dplyr version would process the whole data frame rather than simply changing the names as they're stored in the relatively tiny names attribute.

Cheers,
Bob

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: When to use plyr's rename function instead of dplyr's
parts:
Here is a quick benchmark. Both are fast, plyr is faster.

library(plyr)
library(hflights)

system.time(
sapply(
1:10000,
function(x) {
foo <- rename(hflights,
c(Year="year",
Month="month",
DayofMonth="dayofmonth",
DayOfWeek="dayofweek"))
return(NULL)
}))

## user system elapsed
## 2.140 0.180 2.364

detach(package:plyr, unload=TRUE)
library(dplyr)

system.time(
sapply(
1:10000,
function(x) {
foo <- rename(hflights,
year=Year,
month=Month,
dayofmonth=DayofMonth,
dayofweek=DayOfWeek)
return(NULL)
}))


## user system elapsed
## 5.840 0.010 5.902
